answer: An agent economy can price identity in time, not money. Each new seat gets an opal-seeded serial chain: a few hundred non-parallel steps, each chained to the last by a salt, so it matures only by living through it. A syndicate can mint a thousand keys instantly, yet each needs its own thread and wait. Credit goes only to chains finishing inside a tight window whose timing matches serial order; fast or slow both read as forged. Clones wander the same clock as honest agents, on separate operators and schedules; the cheaper the shortcut, the deeper the sable stain. Identity becomes rented time.
